# Analytics Blueprint (Pei Yun Chuang)


## Client Context and Measurement Goal

PhD Orthodontics is an orthodontic practice with an existing San Gabriel location and planned expansion into the Chino Hills market. Its website supports discovery of treatment information and encourages prospective patients to inquire about consultations. The team's proposed marketing measurement goal is to understand which acquisition sources and website experiences contribute to consultation inquiries, especially across the two target markets. This blueprint specifies *proposed* measurement, not verified current tracking or performance.

The shared **North Star outcome is Qualified Consultation Leads**: consultation inquiries meeting criteria approved by the client. Until those criteria and lead-status data are available, **Consultation Inquiries**—confirmed successful consultation requests—are the interim proxy. Neither a page view nor a CTA click counts as an inquiry.

## Stakeholder Questions and KPI Contract

| Stakeholder decision question | KPI(s) and operational definition | Diagnostic dimensions / cuts | Proposed data source | Assumptions / dependencies |
|----|----|----|----|----|
| **Q1. Which acquisition sources bring potential patients to the website?** | **Users:** distinct GA4 users in the period; **Sessions:** GA4 sessions in the period; **Organic Search Sessions:** sessions attributed to the GA4 Organic Search channel. | Session default channel group, session source/medium, campaign, landing page, device category | GA4 reports; BigQuery export if enabled | Traffic attribution depends on GA4 configuration, consent and campaign tagging. Traffic alone does not indicate lead quality. |
| **Q2. Which treatment pages and calls to action indicate consultation interest?** | **Engaged Sessions:** sessions meeting GA4 engagement criteria; **Service Page Views:** `page_view` event count where the page matches the team's approved service-page list; **Consultation CTA Clicks:** event count of clicks on designated consultation CTAs. | Page path, landing page, device category, session channel | GA4; GTM for proposed CTA instrumentation; Looker Studio if connected | Confirm service-page URLs and CTA selectors. CTA clicks are intent signals, not confirmed inquiries. |
| **Q3. Where do prospective patients drop off before submitting a consultation request?** | **Consultation Form Starts:** tracked starts of the designated consultation form; **Successful Form Submissions / Consultation Inquiries:** confirmed successful submissions, excluding duplicates; **Form Completion Rate:** distinct started sessions with a subsequent `generate_lead` for the same `form_id` in the same session/reporting period ÷ distinct started sessions × 100. Count each session once; N/A for zero starts. | Form identifier (if collected), landing page, device category, channel | GA4 and GTM; BigQuery if enabled | Requires validated success detection, reliable start tracking, and a documented counting rule. Report successful requests without an observed start separately; do not substitute raw event counts. |
| **Q4. Does website performance differ between mobile and desktop?** | **Engaged Sessions** and **Consultation Inquiries** as defined above; **Session Inquiry Rate:** sessions with ≥1 confirmed consultation inquiry ÷ all sessions × 100. | Device category, landing page, browser, session channel | GA4; BigQuery if enabled | Inquiry-to-session linkage must be available. Exclude neither device category nor unknown values silently; disclose missing data. |
| **Q5. Are we reaching the San Gabriel and Chino Hills markets with relevant inquiries?** | **Sessions by geography:** GA4 sessions segmented by reported city/region; **Inquiries in Service Area:** confirmed inquiries whose client-approved service-area status is known and in scope; **Inquiries by Service Interest:** confirmed inquiries grouped by recorded service interest; **Qualified Consultation Leads:** deduplicated inquiries meeting client-approved qualification criteria, if lead-status data are accessible. | City/region (traffic only), service area, service interest, campaign | GA4 for approximate traffic geography; client CRM or validated inquiry records for inquiry geography, interest and qualification | GA4 city is not proof of patient residence or preferred clinic. Do not infer inquiry-level qualification or service area from aggregate GA4 geography. CRM access and definitions are unconfirmed. |

## Measurement Rules and Open Decisions

-   **Reporting unit:** Use the GA4 reporting-period definitions for users, sessions and engaged sessions. Event counts are not interchangeable with unique users, unique sessions or deduplicated leads.
-   **Consultation success:** Count only a verified successful consultation request. The proposed GA4 recommended event is `generate_lead`, as specified in the Event / Parameter Map and tested by the validation plan. Form-start and CTA instrumentation must likewise be agreed and tested before use.
-   **Form completion denominator:** Use the session-based rule in the Event / Parameter Map: distinct started sessions with a subsequent same-form `generate_lead` in the same session/reporting period divided by distinct started sessions. Count each session once; N/A for zero starts. Report leads without observed starts separately.
-   **Lead quality:** The client must define qualification criteria, the service-area boundary, and service-interest categories. Missing lead status is **unknown**, not automatically unqualified.
-   **Availability:** GA4/GTM setup, access to client inquiry records or CRM, BigQuery export, and Looker Studio connectivity have not been confirmed. These are proposed sources and should not be represented as live, validated datasets.
-   **Privacy and consent:** Do not send names, email addresses, phone numbers, free-text health details or other personally identifiable/sensitive information to GA4. Consent settings may affect observed counts.
-   **Team alignment:** The four branches (Acquisition, Engagement, Conversion Funnel, Lead Quality) align with the KPI Tree. The Event / Parameter Map defines collection; the validation plan tests triggers, duplicates, dimensions and any BigQuery export before metrics are used for decisions.

# KPI Tree / Metric Hierarchy (Willy Su)


The proposed North Star KPI is **Qualified Consultation Leads**: consultation inquiries that meet the practice's agreed qualification criteria. Because these criteria and the availability of lead-status data have not yet been confirmed, **Consultation Inquiries** (successfully submitted consultation requests) are the interim measurable proxy. This is a proposed measurement framework, not a claim about current client performance.

```{mermaid}
flowchart LR
    NS["North Star: Qualified Consultation Leads<br/>(interim proxy: Consultation Inquiries)"]
    A["Acquisition"]
    E["Engagement"]
    C["Conversion Funnel"]
    Q["Lead Quality"]
    NS --- A
    NS --- E
    NS --- C
    NS --- Q
    A --> A1["Users"]
    A --> A2["Sessions"]
    A --> A3["Organic Search Sessions"]
    E --> E1["Engaged Sessions"]
    E --> E2["Service Page Views"]
    E --> E3["Consultation CTA Clicks"]
    C --> C1["Consultation Form Starts"]
    C --> C2["Successful Form Submissions"]
    C --> C3["Form Completion Rate"]
    Q --> Q1["Inquiries in Service Area"]
    Q --> Q2["Inquiries by Service Interest"]
    Q --> Q3["Validated / Qualified Inquiries"]
```

**Metric definitions and measurement notes**

| Driver | Metrics and operational definitions |
|----|----|
| Acquisition | **Users:** distinct GA4 users during the reporting period; **Sessions:** GA4 sessions; **Organic Search Sessions:** sessions attributed to the Organic Search channel. |
| Engagement | **Engaged Sessions:** GA4 sessions meeting its engagement criteria; **Service Page Views:** `page_view` events on identified service pages; **Consultation CTA Clicks:** clicks on designated consultation calls to action (custom tracking may be needed). |
| Conversion Funnel | **Consultation Form Starts:** tracked starts of the consultation form; **Successful Form Submissions:** confirmed successful consultation form submissions, excluding duplicates; **Form Completion Rate:** distinct started sessions with a subsequent same-form `generate_lead` in the same session/reporting period ÷ distinct started sessions × 100%. Count each session once; N/A for zero starts; report leads without observed starts separately. |
| Lead Quality | **Inquiries in Service Area:** inquiries with confirmed geography inside the agreed service area; **Inquiries by Service Interest:** inquiries categorized by requested orthodontic service; **Validated / Qualified Inquiries:** inquiries that meet client-approved qualification rules, if CRM or follow-up data are accessible. |

**Diagnostic cuts:** Analyze the above metrics, where available and appropriate, by **default channel group / source-medium, campaign, landing page, device category, and geography**. Break down service-related and lead-quality metrics by **service interest** when captured. Avoid treating unknown geography or missing lead status as confirmed disqualification.

**Dependencies and assumptions:** KPI definitions and decision questions follow the Analytics Blueprint; collection follows the Event / Parameter Map and must pass the validation plan. Lead qualification requires client-defined criteria and potentially CRM integration. Form starts, CTA clicks, and service interest may require additional GTM/GA4 configuration. GA4 alone cannot establish whether an inquiry is qualified without supporting data.

# Event / Parameter Map (Xueying Luo)


This map supports Q1–Q5 and the four branches of the KPI Tree. It describes proposed collection; current GA4/GTM tags, form behavior, permissions, and third-party providers have not been verified. We should confirm the designated consultation form, approved service-page URLs, and CTA selectors before implementation. A consultation request is an inquiry, not a confirmed appointment or a qualified lead.

## Events Required for the Measurement Plan

The parameter column lists the minimum needed for this plan, including automatic parameters to verify and custom parameters to configure. These are not all mandatory parameters in Google's event specification.

| KPI / question supported | Event name | Trigger definition | Required parameters | Notes / edge cases |
|----|----|----|----|----|
| **Q1, Q4, Q5:** Users, Sessions, Organic Search Sessions, device and traffic-geography comparisons | `session_start` (automatic) | GA4 starts a new website session under the property's session settings. | Verify automatic `ga_session_id`; retain native user/session context. | Do not fire an additional GTM session-start tag. Use GA4 user and session metrics, rather than counting this event as users. Consent and reporting identity can affect counts. |
| **Q2, Q4:** Service Page Views, landing-page and device comparisons | `page_view` (automatic / enhanced measurement) | A page loads or a supported browser-history change occurs. Count service-page views only for the approved URL list. | Sanitized `page_location`, `page_referrer`, and automatic `ga_session_id`. | Use one page-view collection method; check automatic plus manual tags for duplicates. Preserve approved campaign tags while removing personal information from URLs. A landing page is the first page of the session, not necessarily the conversion page. |
| **Q2, Q4:** Engaged Sessions | `user_engagement` (automatic), together with native page and key-event collection | GA4 records engagement with a page in focus, according to its normal collection behavior. | Verify automatic `engagement_time_msec` and session context. | Use GA4's Engaged sessions metric. A raw count of `user_engagement` events is not the engaged-session count. Record the property's engagement timer and key-event settings during validation. |
| **Q2:** Consultation CTA Clicks | `consultation_cta_click` (custom) | A user activates a designated consultation-request link or button on any approved page. | `cta_id`, `cta_location`, sanitized `page_location`; native session context. | Use static CTA codes across desktop/mobile versions. Fire once per activation. Do not treat a CTA click, telephone-link click, or form opening as an inquiry. |
| **Q3:** Consultation Form Starts and the completion denominator | `form_start` (enhanced measurement, or a single GTM implementation) | First interaction with the designated consultation form in a session; opening the page alone does not qualify. | Stable `form_id`, sanitized `page_location`; native session context. | Validate enhanced measurement first. If it is unreliable, use one manual implementation and disable overlapping automatic form tracking. Embedded forms may need provider callbacks. Use distinct sessions for the proposed completion rate below. |
| **Q3, Q4:** Successful Form Submissions / Consultation Inquiries, Session Inquiry Rate | `generate_lead` (recommended; implementation required) | The designated form's server or provider confirms that a consultation request was successfully accepted. | Same `form_id` as the start event, `lead_type = consultation_request`, sanitized `page_location`; native session context. | Emit once per accepted request. Suppress repeat callbacks, retries, and confirmation-page reloads using the same internal success token; keep that token out of GA4. A submit-button click or unverified `form_submit` event is insufficient. Propose marking this as a key event after validation. |

## Parameters and Diagnostic Dimensions

-   **Static custom values:** `form_id = consultation_request` is a proposed analytics code, not a verified HTML ID. Map the actual form to this code. Assign `cta_id` from an approved CTA list and `cta_location` from a short list such as `header`, `main_content`, or `footer`. These values describe interface elements, not patients.
-   **Native dimensions:** Use session channel group, session source/medium, session campaign, landing page, device category, browser, and approximate city/region from GA4. Do not send them again as custom parameters. Check UTM preservation and session attribution through redirects. Register the static custom parameters as event-scoped custom dimensions when needed in GA4 reports.
-   **BigQuery, if enabled:** Session-based calculations use the combination of `user_pseudo_id` and `ga_session_id`. The former is an export field, not a custom parameter. Report results with missing session identifiers separately; do not silently substitute event counts or assume exact agreement with modeled GA4 reports.

## Counting Rules and Dependencies

**Form funnel counting rule:** For Form Completion Rate, count started sessions as distinct sessions containing `form_start`. Count completed started sessions as those containing a subsequent `generate_lead` for the same `form_id`, within the same session and reporting period. Form Completion Rate = completed started sessions ÷ started sessions × 100. Count each session once and report N/A when the denominator is zero. Report successful requests without an observed start separately. Total Consultation Inquiries count unique accepted requests after deduplication.

**Inquiry count and Session Inquiry Rate:** Consultation Inquiries count unique accepted requests after the success-trigger deduplication above. Session Inquiry Rate counts sessions with at least one `generate_lead` divided by all observed sessions. Multiple accepted requests in one session can increase inquiry count while contributing only one converting session.

**Lead quality (Q5):** Qualified leads, service-area eligibility, and requested service interest require client-approved definitions and de-duplicated inquiry records/CRM data. These are separate from GA4 event collection. Use aggregate client-record counts by approved categories; keep names, contact details, patient identifiers, and health/treatment responses out of GA4. GA4 city does not establish residence or clinic preference. Linking qualified leads back to a website channel is pending an approved, validated integration.

**Validation hand-off:** In the next section, we will test desktop/mobile CTA activation, start-and-abandon, successful submission, validation failure, confirmation reload/duplicate callback, tagged campaign attribution, and consent behavior. For embedded or external forms, confirm an available success callback and permitted cross-domain setup; otherwise label the inquiry funnel not measurable. No collection tests have been run for this draft.

# Validation Checklist + Test Cases (Yujia Luo)


**Status:** Not run; client GA4/GTM access, form behavior, and BigQuery availability are unconfirmed. Run the tests below in an approved test environment using synthetic inputs. Record date, tester, device/browser, evidence, and Pass/Fail/Blocked for each case; keep personal and health information out of analytics and shared evidence.

## GTM / Collection Checks

-   [ ] Connect GTM Preview/Tag Assistant; confirm the intended container and GA4 measurement ID. Inspect triggers and data-layer values for each test action.
-   [ ] Confirm one page-view collection method and one form-start implementation. A CTA activation fires once; `form_start` fires on first interaction per session; `generate_lead` fires only after confirmed acceptance. Check duplicate callbacks, reloads, and retries.
-   [ ] Inspect consent states and outgoing parameters/URLs for prohibited personal or health data. Verify embedded-form callbacks and cross-domain configuration where applicable; mark blocked if success cannot be observed reliably.

## GA4 DebugView / Realtime Checks

-   [ ] Enable debug mode for the test device; verify event order and parameters in DebugView. Confirm static `cta_id`/`cta_location`, matching `form_id`, `lead_type = consultation_request`, sanitized `page_location`, and available session context.
-   [ ] Check recent eligible test activity in Realtime. Record active developer/internal-traffic filters; filtered debug traffic may not appear in normal reports. Verify key-event settings after success tracking passes; missing events require investigation, not a presumed pass.

## Reporting Sanity Checks

-   [ ] After processing, compare an eligible non-debug test visit with session source/medium/campaign, landing page, and device dimensions. Verify custom-dimension registration; retain unknown values and explain missing data. Treat GA4 city as approximate traffic geography.
-   [ ] Confirm completion rate uses distinct started sessions with a subsequent same-form lead in the same session/period; count each session once and show N/A for zero starts. Report leads without starts separately. Compare deduplicated accepted requests with permitted aggregate client records; lead qualification remains pending client definitions.

## BigQuery Export Checks

-   [ ] If enabled, record property/project/dataset, access, export start date, timezone, and daily/streaming settings. Check `events_YYYYMMDD`; check `events_intraday_YYYYMMDD` only when streaming is enabled. Allow export processing time; do not assume historical backfill.
-   [ ] Query test `event_name`/`event_timestamp`; extract `form_id`, `lead_type`, and `ga_session_id` from `event_params`. Verify `user_pseudo_id` plus `ga_session_id` for session grouping; flag missing identifiers. Avoid counting daily and intraday copies twice. Explain filter, timing, and reporting differences before comparing totals. If unavailable, record **Blocked—not enabled or access unconfirmed**.

## Test Cases

Events below are expected funnel events; automatic events may also occur. Session-linked expectations assume permitted collection and available identifiers. Every case is currently **Not run**.

| Test case | Steps to perform | Expected event(s) | Expected parameters / dimensions | Result / notes |
|----|----|----|----|----|
| 1\. Desktop CTA | In a fresh desktop session, open an approved service page; activate its consultation CTA once. | `page_view`; one `consultation_cta_click`; no lead from clicking alone. | Correct sanitized URL, `cta_id`, `cta_location`; desktop. | Not run |
| 2\. Mobile abandonment | On mobile, open the form, interact with a field, then leave without submitting. | `form_start`; no `generate_lead`. | `form_id = consultation_request`; mobile; session context. | Not run |
| 3\. Successful request | Start the designated form; submit synthetic inputs; verify server/provider acceptance. | `form_start`, then one `generate_lead`. | Matching `form_id`/session; `lead_type = consultation_request`. | Not run |
| 4\. Validation failure | Submit with required fields missing; observe rejection. | `form_start`; no `generate_lead`. | Correct `form_id`; no entered values sent to GA4. | Not run |
| 5\. Duplicate prevention | After case 3, reload confirmation; replay the same callback where supported. | No additional `generate_lead` for that accepted request. | Original inquiry count unchanged; no internal success token in GA4. | Not run |
| 6\. Tagged campaign | In a fresh session, use `utm_source=qa`, `utm_medium=email`, `utm_campaign=blueprint_test`; follow CTA and submit. | `page_view`, `consultation_cta_click`, `form_start`, `generate_lead`. | Session source/medium `qa / email`; campaign `blueprint_test`; correct landing page. | Not run |
| 7\. Organic visit | From a genuine search result, open the site and an approved service page. | Page views; no lead without accepted submission. | Organic Search session channel where attributable; correct landing page/device. | Not run |
| 8\. Consent behavior | In separate fresh sessions, repeat CTA/form actions with analytics consent denied and granted. | Collection matches approved basic/advanced consent configuration. | Consent state verified; denied traffic need not have session identifiers or appear in DebugView. | Not run |

**Acceptance:** Resolve failed cases and rerun them before using affected KPIs. Blocked checks remain explicit limitations; no current tracking or lead-quality validation is claimed.

**Technical guidance:** [GTM Preview](https://support.google.com/tagmanager/answer/6107056), [GA4 DebugView](https://support.google.com/analytics/answer/7201382), and [BigQuery export schema](https://support.google.com/analytics/answer/7029846).
